text: Before approval: Testing mode is limited to 100 test users listed on the consent screen.
quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

text: Before approval: test-user authorizations and refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent.
quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent. If your OAuth client requests an offline access type and receives a refresh token, that token will also expire.
note: Exception: apps requesting only name/email/profile scopes.

text: Before approval: an In-production app requesting unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes shows the unverified app screen.
quote: Google will display an Unverified apps warning message if your project's OAuth clients request authorization of scopes considered sensitive or restricted before your project has completed verification

text: Before approval: unverified apps are capped at 100 new users for the lifetime of the project, and the cap cannot be reset.
quote: Please note the user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed.
note: FAQ also: 'unverified apps that are accessing restricted or sensitive scopes have a 100 new-user cap restriction'.

text: Verify ownership of your authorized domains in Google Search Console.
quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console .

text: Host a public home page and a privacy policy on the same domain, both linked from the consent screen.
quote: The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen of the Google API Console.
note: Home page must be publicly accessible; home page URI is part of consent-screen branding.

text: The privacy policy must disclose how the app accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.
quote: The privacy policy must disclose the manner in which your application accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.

text: Give a written justification for each sensitive scope, including why a narrower scope is not enough.
quote: Prepare a detailed justification for each requested sensitive scope, as well as an explanation for why a narrower scope isn't sufficient.

text: Submit an unlisted YouTube video showing the consent flow, the client ID in the address bar, and each scope in use.
quote: Show that the browser address bar of the OAuth consent screen correctly includes your app's OAuth client ID.
note: Video must also show consent flow (in English) and functionality enabled by each sensitive scope.

text: You must publish your branding before you can request verification for data access.
quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.

text: Restricted Drive scopes are allowed only for backup and sync, productivity and education, or reporting and security apps.
quote: Only specific application types are permitted to use restricted scopes for Google Drive. To qualify, your app must fall into one of the following categories:
note: Categories listed: Backup and sync; Productivity and education; Reporting and security.

text: Apps that store or transmit restricted scope data on servers must pass a security assessment.
quote: If you store restricted scope data on servers (or transmit), then you must go through a security assessment.

text: The assessment uses the App Defense Alliance CASA framework and must be renewed every 12 months.
quote: we are leveraging the industry standard App Defense Alliance and its Cloud App Security Assessment framework (CASA)
note: Page says 'annual'/'every year'; the restricted-scope page states 'at least every 12 months after your assessor's LOA approval date'.

text: Internal-only apps (Workspace-owned project, Internal audience) skip verification and the 100-user cap but only work in that org.
quote: Your app will not be subject to the unverified app screen or the 100-user cap if it's designated as internal-only.  However, only users in the Workspace or Cloud Identity organization will be able
note: Page also notes the app might need approval from an org administrator.

text: drive, drive.readonly, drive.metadata, drive.metadata.readonly, drive.activity and drive.scripts are restricted.
quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive View and manage all your Drive files. https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly
note: All six listed scopes appear under 'Restricted scopes'; the list also includes drive.activity.readonly and drive.meet.readonly.

text: drive.file, drive.appdata and drive.install are non-sensitive; drive.apps.readonly is sensitive.
quote: Sensitive scopes Scope code Description https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.apps.readonly View apps authorized to access your Drive.
note: drive.appdata, drive.install, drive.file are listed under 'Non-sensitive scopes'.

text: drive.file only covers files your app creates or the user opens or picks with your app, not the whole Drive.
quote: Create new Drive files, or modify existing files, that you open with an app or that the user shares with an app while using the Google Picker API or the app's file picker.

text: Google's Trust and Safety team tells you when to start the CASA assessment; it is the last step of the review.
quote: the Google Trust and Safety team will contact you when it is time to initiate the security assessment process.

text: Adding a new restricted scope later may require a new assessment covering it.
quote: If your app adds a new restricted scope, your app might need to be reassessed to cover the additional scope if it wasn't included in a prior security assessment.

text: Google's FAQ estimates sensitive scope verification at 10 business days, which is longer than the 3-5 days on the developer page.
quote: 10 Business days
note: FAQ states 10 business days (estimates not guaranteed); the 3-5 business days figure is on the sensitive-scope-verification developer page, not this FAQ, but was verified there.

text: Limits apply to refresh tokens: 100 per Google Account per client ID, and creating a new one silently invalidates the oldest.
quote: If the limit is reached, creating a new refresh token automatically invalidates the oldest refresh token without warning.
note: Preceding sentence: 'There is currently a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID.'

text: Refresh tokens stop working after 6 months unused or if the user revokes access.
quote: The refresh token has not been used for six months.
note: Page lists several other reasons too (user revoked access, password change with Gmail scopes, token count limit, etc.).

text: Your OAuth redirect URI must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in the Composio auth config; some defaults still use /api/v1/auth-apps/add.
quote: The redirect URI in your OAuth app must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in your Composio auth config. Some toolkit defaults still use https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add

text: Use separate Google Cloud projects for testing and production, and submit only the production project for verification.
quote: Please create separate projects for development/testing/staging and production as per the Google OAuth policy .
note: Page also: 'You should only submit “production” tier projects for verification.'

text: Workspace admins can restrict sensitive scopes to OAuth clients they explicitly mark as trusted.
quote: Google Workspace organization administrators might restrict access to sensitive scopes to prevent access by OAuth client IDs that the organization doesn't explicitly mark as trusted.

text: Google restricted scope verification plus a CASA security assessment (drive.file alone needs no scope review) | wait: Several weeks (Google's FAQ estimates 6 weeks)
quote: the restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete.
fix: Google restricted scope verification, plus a CASA security assessment if the app stores or transmits restricted-scope data on servers | wait: can take several weeks
note: Page makes the CASA assessment conditional on server access/transmission; it does not mention drive.file or the FAQ's 6-week estimate (6 weeks is on the FAQ page; drive.file non-sensitive is on the Drive scopes page).

text: Google charges no fee; the CASA assessor's fee is agreed directly with them
quote: The cost for such a service is agreed on between the developer and the assessor without any involvement from Google.

text: OAuth tokens use the user's rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
quote: OAuth tokens use the user's rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

text: A private GitHub App can only be installed on the account that owns it.
quote: If you set your GitHub App registration to private, it can only be installed on the account that owns the app.

text: Register the app with a name, homepage URL and authorization callback URL.
quote: In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app.
note: Also 'In "Application name", type the name of your app.'

text: Use only information you consider public in the app's fields, since users see them.
quote: Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public. Avoid using sensitive data, such as internal URLs, when creating an OAuth app.
note: The 'since users see them' rationale is not stated explicitly; page frames it as protecting your privacy.

text: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.
quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

text: A GitHub App must be set to 'Any account' (public) before other accounts can install it.
quote: Under "Where can this GitHub App be installed?", select Only on this account or Any account .
note: This page only lists the options; the consequence (private apps install only on the owner account) is stated on the 'Making a GitHub App public or private' page.

text: 'Expire user access tokens' is on by default for new OAuth apps; uncheck it only if your code can't refresh.
quote: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default. If your app's authentication code hasn't been updated to support short-lived tokens, uncheck the box until support is added.

text: Expiring tokens last 8 hours and the refresh token 6 months; each refresh invalidates the old pair.
quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.
note: Also: 'Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old access token will no longer work.'

text: GitHub App user tokens also expire after 8 hours by default; installation tokens expire after 1 hour.
quote: Installation access tokens expire after a predefined amount of time (currently 1 hour).
fix: GitHub App installation tokens expire after 1 hour, and GitHub App user access tokens can expire and be renewed with a refresh token.
note: The page gives the 8-hour figure only for OAuth app user tokens; it does not state an 8-hour default for GitHub App user tokens.

text: Non-expiring OAuth tokens are revoked automatically if unused for one year.
quote: GitHub will automatically revoke an OAuth token or personal access token when the token hasn't been used in one year.
note: Page does not limit this to non-expiring tokens.

text: Only 10 tokens per user/app/scope are kept; creating an 11th revokes an older one.
quote: If an application creates more than ten tokens for the same user and the same scopes, GitHub revokes one of the existing tokens with the same user/application/scope combination

text: New organizations enable OAuth app access restrictions by default, so an org owner must approve your OAuth app.
quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default. Organization owners can disable OAuth app access restrictions at any time.
note: Members request owner approval; privileged OAuth apps are exempt.

text: With a GitHub App, users must install it on their account or org separately; Composio doesn't supply the install link.
quote: Composio does not currently provide the GitHub App installation link automatically during this flow. Provide your GitHub App installation link to the user
note: Text is in the FAQ accordion 'Does Composio support GitHub Apps?' (in page payload).

text: OAuth apps act only as a user; GitHub Apps can also act as the app and get finer-grained permissions.
quote: OAuth apps can only act on behalf of a user while GitHub Apps can either act on behalf of a user or independently of a user. GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions

text: Before approval: a development app links only your own account until you click Enable additional users.
quote: When you first create a Dropbox API app, it’s given development status and can only be connected to your own account.

text: Before approval: a development app can link at most 500 Dropbox users.
quote: it can only be linked with up to 500 total Dropbox users .

text: After 50 linked users you have two weeks to get production approval, or new links are frozen.
quote: once your app links 50 Dropbox users, you will have two weeks to apply for and receive production status approval before your app’s ability to link additional Dropbox users will be frozen

text: The app must follow Dropbox's branding guidelines and terms, or production is rejected.
quote: Before applying for production, make sure your app adheres to the developer branding guidelines and terms and conditions . It will be rejected if it doesn’t.

text: Request the least privileged permissions; Dropbox reviews scope breadth at production.
quote: Your app should use the least privileged permission it can. When applying for production, we’ll review that your app doesn’t request an unnecessarily broad permission

text: The production application asks how the app uses the API and for an app icon.
quote: you’ll be prompted to supply additional information such as how your app uses the API, and to upload an icon for the app.

text: The app name cannot include Dropbox, start with drop, or use DBX or DB.
quote: It can’t begin with “drop”, be similar to Dropbox in sound or spelling, or otherwise refer to Dropbox (for example, don’t use “DBX” or “DB” or “DfB”).

text: Production review does not start until 50 linked users unless you request early review.
quote: it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users
note: Early review possible via the 'Request early review' field.

text: A frozen app can only be unfrozen by getting production approval, not by unlinking users.
quote: for apps that have been temporarily frozen, the only way to unfreeze your app is to apply for and receive production status . Simply unlinking all of your users will not unfreeze your app.

text: You cannot change the app name after production approval.
quote: Keep in mind that once your app has production status, you can’t change its name.

text: Access tokens are short-lived; add token_access_type=offline to get a refresh token.
quote: you’ll need to include token_access_type=offline as a parameter on your Authorization URL in order to return a refresh_token
note: Page describes short-lived access tokens returned with refresh tokens.

text: Redirect URIs must exactly match a registered value in the App Console.
quote: You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the App Console for your application.
note: Dropbox checks the redirect_uri matches one of the registered values at authorization time.

text: Dropbox production status approval | wait: not stated; review starts after 50 linked users
quote: it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users
note: No review duration is stated on the page.

text: Set the integration type to Public to use OAuth; internal integrations only use an API token.
quote: Important: API Key authentication only works with Internal integrations . Public integrations must use OAuth .

text: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS, match exactly, and have no trailing slash, fragment or wildcard.
quote: Must use HTTPS Must match the URI exactly No trailing slash No URL fragments, wildcards, or relative paths

text: Users pick which pages to share during authorization, then press Allow access.
quote: Choose the pages you would like the connection to be able to access, and then press Allow access .
note: Stated under 'Install directly from a partner platform via OAuth'.

text: Notion has no OAuth scopes; access comes from the pages and databases users share.
quote: No. Notion controls access by granting integrations access to specific pages and databases, not through scopes.

text: Actions show the integration's name and logo, not the user's; your own app lets you set them.
quote: The name and logo shown come from the integration configuration. To use a custom name or logo, create your own Notion integration.

text: Connecting the same user again issues a new token pair and can invalidate the older refresh token.
quote: If the same user connects to the same Notion app again, whether it is Composio-managed or custom, Notion can issue a new token pair and invalidate the older refresh_token .
note: Text is in the FAQ 'Reasons for Notion Connection expiry' (page payload).

text: Keep one connection per real user per Notion app to avoid broken refresh tokens.
quote: To avoid this, keep one active Notion connection per real user for a given Notion app

text: A user removing the connection in Settings > Connections revokes the tokens.
quote: If a user removes the Composio-managed or custom Notion app there, the existing token set should be treated as revoked
note: Page says 'Settings -> Connections' and 'should be treated as revoked'.

text: On Enterprise, workspace owners can restrict which connections members may install.
quote: Note: On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can restrict which connections members are allowed to install.

text: With your own app, Notion webhooks need you to paste back a verification token Notion sends to Composio.
quote: Notion sends a verification token to the ingress endpoint, and you paste that token back into Notion to finalize.
